title: Archive exact assignment resident buckets after the 2 GiB screen
question: Do stable resident assignment buckets improve full exact allocation beyond current Auto and explicit Sort on fitting retained parents?
summary: Reject source retention after the declared futility screen. Buckets save 4.1% CPU relative to Auto, take 8.2% longer than Sort and keep temporary traffic equal. One late peer-admission advantage remains in the archived patch.

workloads: 2 GiB and 128 partition parents, per-parent exact unstratified buckets fit at 128 MiB engine, 1 GiB hard no-swap cgroup.
70,003 rows, eight parents, and same fixed peer tests at selection/emission; separate 65,537-row oversize case.

validation.summary: All three complete screen jobs and five small/oversize jobs verify exact fields, quotas, caps, output records, seeded bytes and Analysis. Separate checks cover original retry, cancellation, fixed peer admission and terminal sink denial.

limitations: A single full triplet is a predeclared development futility screen with uncontrolled cache, not a general timing estimate.
The same request at the serializing boundary can admit in buckets and deny under Auto/Sort, with no reduction in the measured complete job peak.
exclusions: Stratified and shuffled exact assignment and the historical probabilistic allocation route.
reopen_when: A workload requiring the measured sink-phase headroom would need an explicit full-job benefit and pressure gate, including oversize retry costs.
